preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 10^4.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and 1 <= n <= 50000 for n in [n_val for n_val, m_val, a_list, k_val, b_list in test_cases])
preconditions.description: For each test case, n is an integer between 1 and 5*10^4.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(m, int) and 2 <= m <= 10**9 for m in [m_val for n_val, m_val, a_list, k_val, b_list in test_cases])
preconditions.description: For each test case, m is an integer between 2 and 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(all(isinstance(x, int) and 1 <= x <= 10**9 for x in a) for a in [a_list for n_val, m_val, a_list, k_val, b_list in test_cases])
preconditions.description: All elements in array a are integers between 1 and 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(k, int) and 1 <= k <= 50000 for k in [k_val for n_val, m_val, a_list, k_val, b_list in test_cases])
preconditions.description: For each test case, k is an integer between 1 and 5*10^4.

preconditions.expression: all(all(isinstance(x, int) and 1 <= x <= 10**9 for x in b) for b in [b_list for n_val, m_val, a_list, k_val, b_list in test_cases])
preconditions.description: All elements in array b are integers between 1 and 10^9.

preconditions.expression: sum(n + k for n, m, a, k, b in test_cases) <= 200000
preconditions.description: The sum of n+k over all test cases does not exceed 2*10^5.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(line.strip().lower() in ['yes', 'no'] for line in stdout_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is either 'Yes' or 'No' (case-insensitive).

postconditions.expression: all((line.strip().lower() == 'yes') == (canonical_form(a, m) == canonical_form(b, m)) for line, (n, m, a, k, b) in zip(stdout_lines, test_cases))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is 'Yes' if and only if the canonical form of array a (under magic number m) is identical to the canonical form of array b. The canonical form is obtained by fully expanding every element into its base components (values not divisible by m) repeated by their multiplicity, then merging adjacent identical values until no further merging is possible, effectively representing the array as a sequence of (value, count) pairs where value is not divisible by m.
